messages:
sara: Quick Q — I'm drafting a small follow-up to the pinning schema RFC. Proposal: add a 'variant coalescence' mode that lets the control plane treat small compatible variant diffs as the same logical pin for routing/telemetry for a configurable window. This would reduce churn for canaries that only change perf/quantization but are behaviorally compatible.

mike: Sounds useful. main risk i see is accidental semantic drift getting hidden. how do we define "compatible"? semantic eval thresholds? :thinking_face:

yun: +1 on the risk. We should require an explicit compatibility signal from the model onboarding step (e.g., delta-accuracy < X on a curated eval set) and attach a coalesce_score. Telemetry needs to still show per-variant traces.

kevin: If we keep per-variant traces, routing still needs a deterministic mapping. Are you proposing a new field in rollout metadata like `coalesce_group_id` and `coalesce_window_days`?

sara: Exactly. Sketch of schema additions:
```
coalesce_group_id: optional string
coalesce_window_days: optional int
coalesce_policy: enum("strict","lenient")
compatibility_signal: {eval_id: string, threshold: float}
```
The control plane would route to the bound variants but tag telemetry with group id. After window expires we either hard-collapse (retire old variant) or lift the group depending on policy.

mike: How does this interact with tenant pins? If a tenant pins to variant A, should coalescing override that? I'd expect tenant pin to take precedence.

lucas: tenant pin precedence seems non-negotiable. But we can auto-suggest tenant migration if coalesce_score is high. e.g., a `suggested_migration` event that the UI shows.

yun: Ops concerns: autoscaler decisions may be affected. If coalesced variants map to the same capacity pool, fine. But if variants live in different quantized hardware pools, we need a fallback mapping rule. Suggest explicit `coalesce_compatible_pools` list in metadata.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary run started for variant v2-quant on release/2026-03-10 :rocket:

kevin: For deprecation flow, propose phases: soft-coalesce (routing+telemetry grouped), notice (notify tenants + suggested migration), hard-deprecate (reject requests with clear error and recommended replacement). Add `deprecation_phase` enum and `deprecation_eta` timestamp.

sara: Good plan. Minimal compatibility contract for coalescing:
- model owner flags compatibility + attaches eval_id and threshold
- platform runs a quick diagnostic from canonical eval set on each variant
- if pass, platform assigns (group_id, coalesce_score)
- coalesce_window starts when first group member is assigned

mike: One more edge: audit & compliance. If customers need immutable model hashes for audit, coalescing must not obscure hashes. Make sure audit logs record the exact variant hash used per inference (even if routed under a group id).

sara: Agreed — audit logs always include variant hash and route decision. UI/telemetry will surface both group and per-variant metrics.

lucas: Implementation notes: lightweight resolver change + rollout metadata extension. Backfill: when enabling for a tenant, we should compute coalesce_group_id deterministically from first variant in group (e.g., sha256 of sorted variant hashes) so behavior is reproducible across control plane replicas.

yun: Also add an opt-out at tenant level: `tenant_meta.allow_coalescing: bool` so regulated customers can decline.

sara: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC + data model PR with fields: coalesce_group_id, coalesce_window_days, coalesce_policy, compatibility_signal, deprecation_phase, deprecation_eta, coalesce_compatible_pools, suggested_migration. Will include example flows and sample UI copy. Link when ready: https://go/redwood/internal/rfc/coalesce (draft)

kevin: Thanks — can you include migration metrics we should capture? success rate, latency delta, cost delta, false-positives where coalesced variant later regressed.

sara: Yep. I'll add telemetry requirements and a playbook for rollback if regression > threshold. Targeting RFC this week. :+1:
